Gallica.definition: Gallica ae, f a Gallic shoe, galosh.

Gallus2.definition: Gallus adj., of Gaul, Gallic, Cs.—As subst m., a Gaul, Cs.—Plur, the Gauls, Cs., C., L.

Gigas.definition: Gigās antis, m , gi/gas, a giant, one of the fabled sons of Earth and Tartarus, O.: fraterculus gigantis, i. e. of obscure birth, Iu.—Plur., C., H., O.

Gorgo.definition: Gorgō onis, f , *gorgw/, a Gorgon; plur. Gorgones, the three daughters of Phorcus, Stheno, Euryale, and Medusa, with beautiful faces, snakes for hair, and a petrifying look, C., V., O., Iu.

Graiugena.definition: Grāiugena ae, m Graius+GEN-, a Grecian by birth, Greek , Pac. ap. C., V.

galla2.definition: galla ae, f a gall-apple, gall-nut (an excrescence on the oak, caused by insects), V.

gallus1.definition: gallus ī, m 1 GAR-, a cock, domestic cock : gallinaceus: gallorum cantus, crowing , H., Iu.

gaudens.definition: gaudēns entis, adj. P. of gaudeo joyful, glad, cheerful : animo gaudenti: Amor, V.

gausape.definition: gausape abl. e, plur. a, n , gausa/phs, a rough woollen cloth: purpureum, H., O.

gelide.definition: gelidē adv. gelidus, coldly, indifferently : ministrare, H.

gelu.definition: (gelū) abl. gelū, frost, cold, ice: membra torrida gelu, L.: gelu Flumina constiterint, H.: Rura gelu tum claudit hiemps, V.: tarda gelu senectus, V.

geminatus.definition: geminātus adj. P. of gemino, twinned, equal : cacumina, L.: consulatūs, consecutive , Ta.

gemmans.definition: gemmāns ntis, adj. P. of gemmo, decked with jewels, jewelled : sceptra, O.

gemmatus.definition: gemmātus adj. P. of gemmo, set with jewels, jewelled : monilia, O.: anulus, L.: pocula, Iu.

genae.definition: genae ārum, f the cheeks: eminentes: exsangues genas: Effusae genis lacrimae, V.: siccat genas, O.: mihi prima genas vestibat flore iuventa, V.: Expilat genis oculos, O.

generaliter.definition: generāliter adv. generalis, in general, generally : definire.

generose.definition: (generōsē) adv. generōsus, nobly .—Only comp: generosius perire, H.

genialiter.definition: geniāliter adv. genialis, jovially, merrily, genially : festum egit, O.

geniculatus.definition: geniculātus adj. geniculum, having knots, hnotted : culmus.

geno.definition: genō —, —, ere GEN-, to beget, bear.—Pass., to be born : si mihi filius genitur, old form. ap. C.; see gigno.

genuinus1.definition: genuīnus adj. GEN-, innate, natural : virtutes.

genuinus2.definition: genuīnus adj. genae, of the cheek : dentes, back-teeth .—As subst m . (sc. dens), Iu.

genus1.definition: genus eris, n GEN-, a race, stock, family, birth, descent, origin : haec Indigna genere nostro, T.: nobili genere nati: amplissimo genere natus, Cs.: generis socia, sister , O.: genere primus: patricium, L.: genus und…

genus2.definition: genus —, n , collat. form of genu, a knee (only nom. and acc.), C. poët.

geometricus.definition: geōmetricus adj. , gewmetriko/s, of geometry, geometrical.—Plur. n. as subst, geometry.

gerens.definition: gerēns ntis, adj. P. of gero, managing, conducting : sui negoti bene.—As subst m. : negoti gerentes, business men .

gesta.definition: gesta ōrum, n P. of gero, deeds, acts, achievements : obscuriora, N.: singulorum, L.

gestamen.definition: gestāmen inis, n gesto, a burden, load, weight : clipeus Abantis, V.: gestamina decent umeros, arms , O.— A litter, sedan , Ta.

gestiens.definition: gestiēns ntis, adj. P. of 2 gestio, unbridled, rapturous, exultant : laetitia: animus rebus secundis, L.: hac (eloquendi vi).

gestio1.definition: gestiō ōnis, f GES-, a managing, performing : negoti.

gestio2.definition: gestiō īvī, —, īre 2 gestus, to gesticulate, express strong feeling, leap, be transported, exult, be joyful, be delighted : sic, T.: cum laetitia gestiat: studio lavandi, V.: voluptate nimiā: otio, L.— To desire eager…

gestus2.definition: gestus ūs, m GES-, bearing, carriage, posture, attitude, motion, gesture, movement, action, sign : vitium in gestu: gestus mihi est capiundus novos, T.: gratificatur mihi gestu: gestum manus Ceycis habebat, O.: nec br…

gignentia.definition: gīgnentia ium, n P. of gigno, productive things, plants : loca nuda gignentium, of vegetation , S.

glans.definition: glāns glandis, f GAL-, an acorn, nut : glande vesci: quae deciderant Iovis arbore glandes, O.: querna, Ta.— An acorn-shaped ball, missile : ex argillā glandes iacere, Cs.: glande pugnare, S.: glande configebantur, L.:…

gloriose.definition: glōriōsē adv. with comp. and sup. gloriosus, gloriously, magnificently : triumphare: alqd gloriosissime conficere.— Boastfully, vauntingly, pompously : exorsus es: mentiri: de me ipso gloriosius praedicare.

gluten.definition: glūten inis, n GLA-, glue, beeswax : collectumque haec ad munera, V.: lentum, V.

grammatica2.definition: grammatica ōrum, n , grammatika/, grammar, philology.

grande.definition: grande adv. n of grandis, loudly : sonare, Iu.

granditer.definition: (granditer) adv. grandis, loftily .—Only comp: grandius sonare, O. (dub.).

grate.definition: grātē adv. with comp. gratus, with pleasure, agreeably, gladly, willingly : praeterita meminit: Natalīs numeras, H.: Gratius ex fonte bibuntur aquae, O.— Thankfully, gratefully : alqd facere.

gratiis.definition: grātiīs adv. abl plur. of gratia, without reward, for nothing, gratis : si non pretio, gratiis, T.

gratis.definition: grātīs adv. for gratiis, out of favor, through kindness, without recompense, without pay, for nothing, gratuitously, gratis : frumentum dare: ne gratis in provinciā male audires: rei p. servire: praetor factus est.

gratuito.definition: grātuītō adv. gratuitus, without pay, for naught, gratis, gratuitously : causas defendens: civitatem impertire, for no particular reason : crudelis erat, wantonly , S.

gratulator.definition: (grātulātor ōris), m gratulor, one who congratulates (in a spurious passage).

gravanter.definition: gravanter adv. gravans, reluctantly : venire, L.

gravate.definition: gravātē adv. gravatus, with difficulty, reluctantly, unwillingly, grudgingly : non gravate respondere: ille primo: concedere, L.

grave.definition: grave adv. gravis, strongly, rankly : olens, V.

graviter.definition: graviter adv. with comp. gravius, and sup. gravissimē gravis, weightily, heavily, ponderously : tela ut gravius acciderent, Cs.: cecidi. O.—Of tone, deeply : sonare: sonat ungula cornu, V.— Vehemently, strongly, viole…

gravor.definition: gravor ātus, ārī, dep. pass. of gravo, to be burdened, feel incommoded, be vexed, take amiss, bear with reluctance, regard as a burden, hesitate, do unwillingly : ne gravere, T.: gravari coepit, quod, etc.: ego vero n…

gressus2.definition: gressus ūs, m GRAD-, a stepping, going, step, course, way : tendere gressum ad moenia, V.: conprime gressum, V.: presso gressu, slowly , O.: gressūs glomerare superbos, V.: huc dirige gressum, i. e. steer , V.

grunditus.definition: grūndītus (grūnnītus) ū s, m grunnio, a grunting : suis.

grus.definition: grūs (nom. gruis, Ph.), gruis, m and f 1 GAR-, a crane , C., V., O.; a delicacy, H.

gryps.definition: grȳps grȳpis, m , gru/y, a griffin (a fabulous four-legged bird).—Prov.: Iungentur iam grypes equis (of an impossibility), V.

gurgulio.definition: gurguliō ōnis, m GVOR-, the gullet, weasand, windpipe .

gustatus.definition: gustātus ūs gusto, the taste, sense of taste : gustatus, qui sentire debet, etc.— A taste, flavor : pomorum iucundus: (uva) peracerba gustatu.— Fig., flavor, enjoyment : verae laudis.

gypsatus.definition: gypsātus adj. with sup. gypsum, covered with gypsum, plastered : gypsati crimen pedis, chalked for sale (as a slave), O., Tb.: manibus gypsatissimis (of an actor in a woman's part).
